context:
Follow the TimescaleDB pattern (benchbox/platforms/timescaledb.py) with key
differences in schema creation:

1. Create PgMooncakeAdapter(PostgreSQLAdapter) in benchbox/platforms/pg_mooncake.py
2. Override create_connection() to verify pg_mooncake extension is installed
3. Override create_schema() to modify DDL: add "USING columnstore" to
   CREATE TABLE statements. This is the critical difference - tables must use
   the columnstore access method for pg_mooncake to activate.
4. Inherit load_data() from PostgreSQLAdapter - COPY works on columnstore
   tables but internally creates Parquet files
5. Override configure_for_benchmark() for pg_mooncake-specific GUCs
6. Register in platform_registry.py with metadata (category: "olap-columnstore",
   platform_family: "pg_mooncake")

For the DDL generator (benchbox/core/tuning/generators/pg_mooncake.py),
extend PostgreSQLDDLGenerator and add USING columnstore to all CREATE TABLE
statements. Handle unsupported data types by mapping them to supported types
or raising clear errors.

Storage configuration:
- Default: local disk (simplest for benchmarking)
- Optional: S3/GCS backend via mooncake.default_bucket GUC
- CLI flags: --mooncake-storage=local|s3 --mooncake-bucket=<url>
description:
Add a pg_mooncake platform adapter that enables benchmarking PostgreSQL with
the pg_mooncake extension installed. pg_mooncake adds native columnstore
tables (Iceberg/Delta Lake backed, Parquet storage) with DuckDB-powered
vectorized execution to PostgreSQL, achieving top-10 ClickBench performance.

Unlike pg_duckdb which accelerates queries on regular heap tables,
pg_mooncake uses a custom "columnstore" table access method (CREATE TABLE ...
USING columnstore) that stores data in Parquet format with Iceberg metadata.
This gives true columnar compression (5:1 to 20:1) and DuckDB-native
execution on columnar data.

This adapter should inherit from PostgreSQLAdapter and override schema
creation to use columnstore tables, handle the different data loading path
(COPY into columnstore creates Parquet files), and configure pg_mooncake-
specific GUC parameters.

Key benchmarking scenarios:
- pg_mooncake columnstore vs PostgreSQL heap tables (same queries)
- pg_mooncake vs native DuckDB (columnar vs columnar)
- pg_mooncake vs ClickHouse (ClickBench comparison - pg_mooncake is top 10)
- pg_mooncake with object storage backend (S3/GCS) vs local disk

anti_patterns.dont: bundle or install pg_mooncake via the adapter
anti_patterns.instead: only verify it exists and raise a clear error if missing
anti_patterns.why: extension installation requires server admin privileges and Docker setup

anti_patterns.instead: override in the pg_mooncake adapter class
anti_patterns.why: pg_mooncake needs USING columnstore only for its own tables

anti_patterns.dont: silently fall back to heap tables on unsupported types
anti_patterns.instead: raise a clear error listing which columns have unsupported types
anti_patterns.why: this would produce misleading benchmark results

anti_patterns.dont: try to ALTER existing heap tables to columnstore in-place
anti_patterns.instead: create tables with columnstore from the start
anti_patterns.why: pg_mooncake requires CREATE TABLE ... USING columnstore
